originality.rationale: Hedenmalm and Zhu (1992, Propositions 2–4) explicitly analyze the ONE-point weighted-Bergman extremal via roots of unity, including the α>4 threshold. That half-plane criterion is PRIOR mathematics and not claimed new. The new statement is the exact TWO prescribed antipodal zeros, two interacting kernel singularities, fully counted simple nonreal quartet roots and borderline branch classification. Felder–Le (2021), Cheng–Mashreghi–Ross (2018), Le (2019) and older canonical-divisor texts do not state the same quantified two-point result in inspected material. Historical priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: The root-of-unity half-plane threshold for a ONE-point divisor is known (Hedenmalm–Zhu 1992). The new theorem determines the complete zero count for the simplest symmetric TWO-point divisor, including how its two singular kernel terms interact, prove all roots simple/nonreal except prescribed, and settle exact tangent cases. It is an independently meaningful canonical-divisor zero-geometry classification, though closely related to the earlier one-site result.
